the following:
 Judgment

The appellants/claimants have filed this Misc. Appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act (in short "the Act") assailing the award passed by the learned 3rd Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur, in Claim Case No.600269/2015 on 21.01.2017, whereby an award of Rs.14,19,890/- along with 7% interest from the date of filing of the claim petition i.e. 03.07.2015 has been passed.

entities.text: 3rd Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The facts necessary for disposal of the present appeal in brief are that on 23.06.2015 at about 9:15 am, after completing his work, deceased Lekhram Sahu was going to the his house on his motorcycle from Bhandari Hospital, when he reached Gulati Chouraha respondent No.1 was driving the car bearing No. MP-22-M-9999, with rashly and negligently and dashed to the motorcycle of deceased.
Due to which the appellant fall down from his motorcycle and received grievous injury and ultimately he succumbed to the injuries.

3. The contentions before this court raised by the learned counsel for the appellants are that the learned claims tribunal has not awarded any amount in the head of future prospects and loss of estate which should have been awarded in the light of judgment passed by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017(16) SCC 680.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017(16) SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the respondent No.3/insurance company has opposed the prayer drawing attention of this Court towards the amount awarded by the learned claims tribunal in the head of loss of consortium which is 1,00,000/- in the instant case.
Without filing any cross objection or cross appeal it has been faintly contended that award amount is in the higher side and it should be reduced.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the impugned award along with record.
6.

Since no cross appeal or cross objection has been filed by the respondent No.3/insurance Company, therefore, the contentions regarding reducing the awarded amount specifically in the head of loss of consortium cannot be sustained.

7. In para graph 59.4 of the judgment In the case of Pranay Sethi (Supra), summarizing the conclusions it has been held that future prospects be awarded as per age and nature of the employment of the deceased.

The para 59.4 of the judgment in the case of Pranay Sethi (Supra)
which reads as under:-
"In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

The established income means the Smt. Meena Sahu vs Mehbub Khan on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21002844/
2 income minus the tax component."
8.

entities.text: Smt. Meena Sahu vs Mehbub Khan on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the light of above judgment, contention raised on behalf of the appellants has substance as no amount has been awarded in the head of future prospects.
9. In the instant case, age of the deceased was admittedly in the age group of 41 to 45 and the deceased was on a fixed salary an addition of 25% in the head of future prospects is to be awarded.
The calculation of total compensation will be as under:-

Sr . Head Compensation awarded No.
1 Yearly income (as taken by Rs. 1,32,000/-
 claims tribunal)
2 Future prospect 25% Rs. 33,000/-
3 Deduction towards personal Rs. 55,000/-
 expenses (1/3rd of Rs. 1,32,000  + 33,000 =1,65,000/-
4 Total annual income (Rs. Rs. 1,10,000/-
 1,65,000- Rs. 55,000/-)
5.

After applying multiplier of 14 Rs. 15,40,000/-
(Rs. 1,10,000/- x 14), total loss of dependency 10.
In the case of Pranay Sethi (supra) in paragraph 59.8, the Hon'ble Apex Court has directed to awarded amount of Rs. 15,000/- in the head of loss of estate.
Since claims tribunal has failed to give any amount in this head, for just and proper compensation, this amount of Rs. 15,000/- is also to be added.

11. Thus, loss of dependency will be taken as Rs. 15,40,000/- as against the amount of Rs.
12,32,000/- awarded by the claims tribunal.

Difference of amount comes to Rs.3,08,000/- and for loss of estate, claimants are also entitled for Rs. 15,000/-.
12.
Thus, appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs. 3,23,000/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
13. Resultantly, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.3,23,000/-.

The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Smt. Meena Sahu vs Mehbub Khan on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21002844/
3 Tribunal.
